items.stem: A shipment is low value per kilogram, not time-critical, and moves across an ocean. Which mode is usually most appropriate?

options.rationale: Correct: for low value density and non-urgent cross-ocean moves, sea freight offers the lowest cost per unit.
Air is fast but far costlier, unjustified for low-value, non-urgent goods.
Road cannot cross an ocean and expedited service adds needless cost.
Parcel courier suits small urgent items, not bulk low-value ocean cargo.

items.explanation: Correct: for low value density and non-urgent cross-ocean moves, sea freight offers the lowest cost per unit.

items.stem: Under Incoterms, which TWO points are defined by the chosen term? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Where risk of loss or damage transfers from seller to buyer
options.rationale: Correct: each Incoterm fixes the point where risk passes.

options.text: Which party arranges and pays for carriage to a point
options.rationale: Correct: Incoterms allocate transport cost and arrangement responsibilities.

options.text: The retail selling price of the goods
options.rationale: Incoterms do not set the product's market price.
Quality specs are defined in the contract of sale, not by Incoterms.

items.explanation: Correct: each Incoterm fixes the point where risk passes.

items.stem: Two carriers have the same average transit time, but one varies far more day to day. Why does the lower-variability carrier often give better service?

options.text: Reliability (low variability) improves on-time performance and planning
options.rationale: Correct: consistent transit times let customers and planners meet windows; averages hide reliability.

options.text: A higher average always means better service
options.rationale: The averages are equal here; variability is the differentiator.

options.text: Variability has no effect on on-time delivery
options.rationale: High variability directly causes missed delivery windows.

options.text: Lower variability always means lower cost
options.rationale: Reliability and cost are related but not identical; the benefit here is service.

items.explanation: Correct: consistent transit times let customers and planners meet windows; averages hide reliability.
